item.aggregated_output:
# Tensile test analysis

## Method

Stress was regressed against strain separately for each material using all 30 measurements (three specimens × ten strain levels) and an ordinary least-squares line with a free intercept. The slope is the estimated elastic modulus; 1 MPa per unit strain equals 0.001 GPa. The specimen-level slope spread is shown as sample standard deviation (n = 3).

## Results

| Material | Pooled modulus (GPa) | Fit intercept (MPa) | R² | Mean specimen slope ± SD (GPa) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Aluminum | 69.38 | -0.31 | 0.99834 | 69.38 ± 1.76 |
| Steel | 199.06 | 0.62 | 0.99844 | 199.06 ± 2.00 |
| Titanium | 116.56 | -0.77 | 0.99788 | 116.56 ± 1.71 |

## Figure

![Stress–strain measurements and pooled linear fits](stress_strain_fits.svg)

## Interpretation

The fitted slopes rank steel highest, followed by titanium and aluminum. The pooled lines describe the observed range (strain 0.0002–0.0020); the supplied file does not identify a separately selected elastic region, so these are range-wide linear estimates. The high R² values indicate that a straight line captures most of the variation over this range, while specimen-level slopes summarize the observed replicate variation.
